Where the idea came from

My team’s research into specialized AI models for healthcare administration involved conversations with professionals, executives, researchers, and technical decision makers. We wanted to understand operational problems and the reliability limits of existing systems before choosing a product opportunity.

Echo explores an asynchronous format: participants answer through WhatsApp voice notes while an AI interviewer asks relevant, neutral follow-up questions.

My contribution

I defined the participant journey and requirements for conversational pathways, consent, participant controls, and reviewable decisions. With AI coding assistance, I translated those requirements into a backend and researcher workspace while learning the architecture.

A researcher edits and approves a guide, then creates an invitation. The intended participant flow explains AI use, collects consent, and accepts text or voice answers. The backend retrieves and normalizes audio, requests transcription and structured analysis, saves the result, and queues the next question.

A deliberate boundary for the model

The model supplies analysis; application code controls consent, transitions, follow-up limits, and sending. Durable records preserve progress across messages and restarts. Pause, withdrawal, and support requests take precedence over questioning. Duplicate detection and durable message processing address delivery failures without assuming a repeated send is harmless.

What has been verified

The recorded checks include 132 backend tests, 10 dashboard gateway tests, type checking, a production build, and a restricted cloud database connection. Offline interview tests replace Meta and OpenAI with test doubles.

A real WhatsApp voice interview and live transcription quality remain unverified. The next milestone is a consented real-device test followed by review of follow-up relevance, neutrality, and objective coverage. Hosted access and commercial platform eligibility also need verification.

The intended journey

A conversation with structure

  1. Approve the guideResearch objectives, questions, and limits.
  2. Invite and obtain consentAI disclosure before the interview begins.
  3. Listen and follow upVoice or text, with bounded adaptation.
  4. Review the evidenceTranscripts, coverage, and decision records.

Implemented flow; live-provider validation is still pending.
